subject: System Design
title: Discord's Voice Architecture
description: A 60-second lesson on Discord's Voice Architecture.

hook.text: 200 people in a Discord voice channel, all talking and listening simultaneously. That's 200 audio streams to mix.

buildup.text: Discord uses selective forwarding: instead of mixing audio on the server, it sends individual streams to each client.

discovery.text: Clients decide which streams to prioritize. Active speakers get full quality; silent users get minimal bandwidth.

twist.text: Voice data uses UDP, not TCP. Lost packets are acceptable — a tiny glitch is better than waiting for a retransmission.

climax.text: Discord's voice system prioritizes low latency over perfection: fast and slightly imperfect beats slow and perfect.

punchline.text: Forward audio selectively — low latency beats perfect quality.

quiz.question: Why does Discord voice use UDP instead of TCP?
options: Lost packets cause tiny glitches, which is better than retransmission delays
